technical_principles.summary: Neutral offense and defense start from a balanced stance with loaded hips, bent knees, head up, hands ready, and feet able to move without crossing.
Motion should change angle, distance, and pressure while preserving stance; crossing feet, standing tall, and reaching without foot movement expose attacks.
A shot is built by lowering the hips and bending the knees before penetration, then driving up and through the opponent rather than diving forward.
Shot mechanics should preserve head up, back straight, hips in, knees off the mat when finishing, and toe pressure for drive.
Hand fighting is purposeful: create angle, break posture, clear blocks, win inside position, capture wrists, force a reaction, or connect a tie to an attack.
A tie is valuable only when it improves position or opens offense; athletes should learn tie entries, pressure direction, clears, and immediate attacks from the tie.
A collar tie should control posture without hanging; elbow position, head pressure, and foot motion prevent the tie from becoming a stagnant or vulnerable position.
Inside tie position controls the centerline and can steer the opponent into snaps, singles, high crotches, duck unders, and underhook entries.
Wrist control can deny the opponent's tie, open their elbow line, create arm drag/two-on-one entries, or clear a path for leg attacks.
Two-on-one control works best when the attacker controls wrist/elbow or wrist/upper arm, steps to an angle, keeps posture, and attacks before the opponent squares up.
Underhook offense needs head position, hip proximity, opponent posture control, and foot motion; static underhooks invite whizzers, squares, and counters.
source_refs: USA Wrestling Rule Book and Guide to Wrestling

technical_principles.summary: The overhook/whizzer is both defense and counteroffense: apply hip pressure, square or angle out, block the opponent's head/shoulder line, and look to go behind, limp-leg, throw-by, or reattack.
source_refs: United World Wrestling International Wrestling Rules

technical_principles.summary: Front headlock scoring depends on controlling head-and-arm alignment, keeping chest pressure through the opponent, circling to an angle, and preventing the opponent from peeking out or reshooting.
Singles, doubles, high crotches, low singles, and ankle picks should be entered from a setup, level change, and angle rather than from reaching or shooting from too far away.
Finishing requires continuing through the opponent, improving head/hip position, coming up when appropriate, cutting angles, and transitioning immediately to control or exposure.
source_refs: United World Wrestling International Wrestling Rules

technical_principles.summary: Intermediate and advanced neutral wrestling is organized as attack, opponent reaction, finish, reattack, or counter-to-counter rather than one isolated move.
Takedown defense begins with head, hands, and hips: block the entry, keep hips away, square or angle out, and convert defense into a circle, go-behind, or reattack.
Folkstyle rewards control, freestyle rewards exposure and rapid continuation, and Greco-Roman forbids leg attacks; neutral teaching must filter techniques by rule set.
source_refs: USA Wrestling Rule Book and Guide to Wrestling
United World Wrestling International Wrestling Rules

beginner.teaching_style: Short technical blocks, high repetition, cooperative partner feeds, game-based movement, clear safety stops, and limited live goes.
readiness_markers: changes level without bending at waist

avoid_until_ready: advanced scramble sequences without position gates
intermediate.teaching_style: Situational drilling from common reactions, constrained live wrestling, two- and three-step chains, and immediate transition to control after takedown.

avoid_until_ready: adding techniques that dilute primary scoring system
advanced.teaching_style: Individualized technical-tactical models, film-informed constraints, high-intensity situational goes, pressure testing under clock/score, and attack systems refined by body type and rule set.
readiness_markers: chooses tactics by score and boundary

drills_or_practice_design.goal: Build stance integrity while moving and changing levels.
drills_or_practice_design.format: Solo or partner mirror; shuffle, circle, stance check, level change, downblock cue, reset.

drills_or_practice_design.goal: Lower level under pressure without folding at the waist.
drills_or_practice_design.format: Partner pressures shoulders; athlete drops hips/knees, keeps posture, and penetrates to position.

drills_or_practice_design.goal: Connect hand clear to penetration for doubles, singles, and high crotches.
drills_or_practice_design.format: Pop or clear opponent elbows, step in, make upper-body contact, and finish to controlled position.
Partner reaches or shoots; athlete downblocks or crossblocks, reloads legs, and immediately reattacks.

drills_or_practice_design.goal: Build baseline takedown defense and scoring conversion.
drills_or_practice_design.format: Partner shoots; defender sprawls, pressures head/shoulder line, circles, covers hips, and secures control.

drills_or_practice_design.goal: Connect snap down to front headlock control and go-behind.
drills_or_practice_design.format: From collar/inside tie, snap to head-and-arm control, circle to angle, block near arm, cover hips.

drills_or_practice_design.goal: Prevent passive hand fighting and teach immediate offense after clearing ties.
drills_or_practice_design.format: Partner applies collar, wrist, inside tie, or underhook; athlete clears to preferred tie and attacks within two beats.

drills_or_practice_design.goal: Teach Russian tie control as an attack system.
drills_or_practice_design.format: Enter two-on-one from wrist/inside tie, step to angle, drill arm drag, single, duck, snap, or mat return-safe finish by rule set.
coaching_cues: do not pull from square stance

drills_or_practice_design.goal: Teach underhook offense and whizzer defense as linked decisions.
drills_or_practice_design.format: One athlete starts underhook, other whizzers; attacker works knee pick, high crotch, body lock, or throw-by while defender squares, hips in/out, circles, or reattacks.
coaching_cues: stop if shoulder is twisted under load
source_refs: United World Wrestling International Wrestling Rules

drills_or_practice_design.goal: Build finish resilience after first defense.
drills_or_practice_design.format: Attacker enters single/double/high crotch; defender gives scripted reactions; attacker progresses through finish options.

drills_or_practice_design.goal: Develop retention and match decision-making through constrained games.
drills_or_practice_design.format: Small games such as win inside tie, score from front headlock, defend-and-reattack, or finish from single within boundary/time constraints.
coaching_cues: coach the rule of the game
pause only for safety or repeated error

common_errors.correction: Lower hips and knees while keeping head up and feet active.
common_errors.risk: Late defense, easy leg attacks, weak hand fighting.

common_errors.error: Reaching with arms before moving feet.
common_errors.correction: Close distance with stance motion, head/hand position, and angle before tie or shot.
common_errors.risk: Arm drags, posts, snap downs, and exposed lead leg.

common_errors.correction: Use short shuffle and circle steps that keep hips loaded.
common_errors.risk: Loss of balance and poor sprawl reaction.

common_errors.error: Changing level by folding at the waist.
common_errors.correction: Drop hips with knee bend and maintain straight back.
common_errors.risk: Front headlock, neck pressure, failed penetration.

common_errors.error: Shooting without setup or from outside effective distance.
common_errors.correction: Use tie, motion, fake, snap, or wrist clear to enter at closer range.

common_errors.error: Attacking with head down or eyes to mat.
common_errors.correction: Keep head up and back straight through entry and finish.
common_errors.risk: Neck stress, stuffed head, poor drive.

common_errors.error: Hanging in collar tie without foot motion or attack.
common_errors.correction: Use snap, circle, elbow control, wrist capture, or clear to next tie.

common_errors.error: Pulling two-on-one while square in front of opponent.
common_errors.correction: Step to angle and attack before opponent squares or peels.

common_errors.error: Underhooking without head and hip position.
common_errors.correction: Win head position, move feet, and control opponent posture before attacking.
common_errors.risk: Whizzer counter, throw-by, body lock exposure.

common_errors.error: Sprawling and stopping without circling or scoring.
common_errors.correction: Apply hip/chest pressure, circle to angle, and cover hips or reattack.
common_errors.risk: Opponent recovers to second shot or chain finish.

common_errors.error: Trying to muscle a finish before improving head, hip, and angle.
common_errors.correction: Rebuild position, cut corner, come up, or transition to a safer finish.

common_errors.error: Stopping after the takedown rather than controlling or attacking exposure/top position.
common_errors.correction: Practice finish-to-control and finish-to-turn windows by rule set.
common_errors.risk: Lost control in folkstyle or missed par terre/exposure opportunity in freestyle/Greco.

safety_constraints.constraint: Progress from solo movement to cooperative partner feed to constrained live before full live wrestling.
safety_constraints.rationale: Controls injury risk while preserving technical quality under increasing pressure.
source_refs: USA Wrestling Athlete Development Model Poster

safety_constraints.constraint: Do not allow repeated head-down shots, neck cranks, forced front headlock pressure, or uncontrolled bridge loads.
safety_constraints.rationale: Neutral attacks and front-headlock positions can stress the cervical spine when posture collapses.

safety_constraints.constraint: Teach upper-body throws, back steps, lifts, and mat returns only with qualified supervision, adequate mat space, and breakfall/base readiness.
safety_constraints.rationale: High-amplitude or poorly controlled landings increase shoulder, neck, and head risk.
source_refs: United World Wrestling International Wrestling Rules

safety_constraints.constraint: Stop or scale whizzer/overhook drills when the shoulder is forced behind the athlete, twisted under load, or paired with uncontrolled rotation.
safety_constraints.rationale: Defensive positions during takedowns are common mechanisms for shoulder stress.

safety_constraints.constraint: Low single, ankle pick, and finish drills must avoid twisting the defender's knee with trapped foot and uncontrolled lateral force.
safety_constraints.rationale: Leg attacks and defensive reactions can load the knee when foot, hip, and knee lines are trapped.

safety_constraints.constraint: Block leg attacks in Greco-Roman profiles and flag techniques illegal or unsafe for the selected rule set, age group, or competition modifications.
safety_constraints.rationale: Rule-set mismatch creates unsafe habits and illegal scoring attempts.
source_refs: United World Wrestling International Wrestling Rules
USA Wrestling Rule Book and Guide to Wrestling

safety_constraints.constraint: End or regress neutral live goes when stance collapses, head drops, shots become dives, or partners cannot return safely to position.
safety_constraints.rationale: Technique degradation under fatigue increases injury risk and reinforces low-quality patterns.
source_refs: USA Wrestling Athlete Development Model Poster

sport_training_rules.title: Teach neutral basics before open live takedowns
Require level change before leg attack entry
Hand fighting must create a scoring action or positional advantage
Neutral defense should convert to go-behind or reattack
Every takedown finish must transition by rule set
